answer: A radio horizon protocol curbs Sybil attacks among autonomous agents operating between an orchard and a coastal jetty. Verifiers exchange time-of-flight RF pulses across the horizon to triangulate each transmitter's physical coordinates. An attacker incurs the verifiable cost of deploying dedicated radio transceivers across distinct geographic positions per identity. However, multipath reflections from wet foliage or sea spray distort propagation timing, causing false rejections.
